rules.title: How to play
rules.hubIntro: New here? Start with Learn to play: it takes about 2 minutes.
rules.newHere: New to the game? Learn in 2 minutes

slides.title: Last one standing wins
slides.body: Everyone has 2 face-down cards, and each card is a life. Lose them all and you're out. The last player left wins.

slides.title: Your cards
slides.body: The deck has 5 characters, 3 cards each. You're dealt 2 cards, and only you can see them.

slides.title: Taels
slides.body: Everyone starts with 2 {currency}. Money pays for Assassinate (3 {currency}) and Coup (7 {currency}).

slides.title: One action a turn
slides.body: On your turn, pick exactly 1 action. Then it's the next player's turn.

slides.title: Anyone can do these
slides.body: Income: +1. Foreign aid: +2, but {duke} can block it. Coup: pay 7 and someone loses a card; nobody can block it. With 10+ {currency} you must Coup.

slides.title: Claim a character
slides.body: To use a character's power, you claim you have that card, true or not. Claiming one you don't have is a bluff: that's the game, not cheating.

slides.title: Challenge!
slides.body: Anyone can challenge a claim. No such card: caught, and the claimer loses a card. The real thing: the challenger loses a card, and the claimer draws a new one.

slides.title: Block
slides.body: {duke} blocks foreign aid. {captain} and {ambassador} block stealing. {contessa} blocks assassination. A block is a claim too, so it can be challenged.

slides.title: Losing a card
slides.body: When you lose a life, you choose which of your cards to turn face up. Face-up cards are public, and the Cards out tally counts them for you.

slides.title: Ready!
slides.body: That's enough to play. To check something later, open the rules reference.

overview.title: Overview
items: 2–6 players. Goal: be the last player with a face-down card.
The deck has 15 cards: 5 characters × 3. Everyone is dealt 2 face-down cards and 2 {currency}.
In a 2-player game the first player starts with only 1 {currency}, to balance going first.
The first player is chosen at random; turns then go around the table.

assassin.action: Assassinate: pay 3 {currency}, someone loses a card

captain.action: Steal: take up to 2 {currency} from someone

ambassador.action: Exchange: draw 2 cards, keep as many as you have face down, return the rest

actions.title: General actions
items: Income: +1 {currency}. Can't be blocked or challenged.
Foreign aid: +2 {currency}. Anyone may claim {duke} to block it.
Coup: pay 7 {currency}, someone loses a card. Can't be blocked or challenged.
With 10+ {currency} at the start of your turn, you must Coup.
You can't pick an action you can't afford. Costs are paid as you claim.
Actions that target someone can only target players still in the game.

challenge.title: Challenge
items: Anyone still in the game can challenge a character claim, even if they aren't the target. If several want to, only the first challenge counts.
If the claimer doesn't have the card, they're caught: they lose a card and the action (or block) fails. For an action, what they paid is refunded.
If they do have it, the challenger loses a card. The claimer shuffles the proven card into the deck, draws a new one themselves, and the action goes ahead.
Income, foreign aid and coup claim no character, so they can't be challenged.

block.title: Block
items: Only these can be blocked: foreign aid (by anyone, with {duke}), assassination (only by the target, with {contessa}), stealing (only by the target, with {captain} or {ambassador}).
A block is a character claim, so anyone can challenge it, including the player who acted.
A block can't be blocked.
A successful block stops the action, but what was paid stays paid: a blocked assassination still costs 3 {currency}.
A block caught as a bluff: the blocker loses a card and the action goes ahead.

influence.title: Losing cards
items: When you lose a card, you choose which one to turn face up. With one face-down card left, that one turns.
Face-up cards stay on the table for everyone to see and can't be used again.
No face-down cards left means you're out: your money goes back, you get no turns and can't challenge or block.
You can lose 2 cards in one turn. For example: being assassinated after a wrong challenge, or being assassinated after a {contessa} bluff is caught.
If the target is out before the action happens, the action does nothing more; costs aren't refunded.

timers.title: Timers
items: Challenging or blocking, and choosing cards, have time limits set by the pace (Relaxed, Normal, Fast). When time runs out it counts as passing, or a card is chosen for you.
Against bots there's no time limit to pick an action. In online rooms the host picks Off, 30 s, 60 s or 2 minutes; when time runs out you take Income (or Coup if you must).
Drawing a new card after winning a challenge: 15 seconds, then one is drawn at random.

items.q: Assassinated without {contessa}: should I claim {contessa} to block?
items.a: You can, it's a bluff. But if it's challenged and caught, you lose a card for the bluff and are still assassinated: both cards in one go. With one card left you lose anyway if you don't block, so the bluff costs nothing more.

items.q: If my challenge is wrong, does the other player lose anything?
items.a: No. They shuffle the proven card into the deck and draw a new one; you lose a card.

items.q: Can players who aren't targeted challenge?
items.a: Yes. Anyone still in the game can challenge any claim, actions and blocks alike.
No, foreign aid claims no character. But anyone may claim {duke} to block it, and that block can be challenged.

items.q: What if I steal from someone with only 1 {currency}?
items.a: You take that 1 {currency}: stealing takes up to 2, never more than they have.
